svg.title: A Nested Annual Cohort Supporting the Base Case
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-02-renewal-cohort-funnel; chart type: funnel; title: A Nested Annual Cohort Supporting the Base Case; subtitle: 200 permissioned opportunities narrow to 10 activated portfolio accounts.; chapter number: 6; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Illustrative annual acquisition cohort, not measured conversion data. Each stage is a subset of the preceding stage. Ten portfolio accounts each contribute $50,000 in annual recognized retained revenue after full activation; partial-year activation produces less revenue.; caption: Stage conversions are 50%, 50%, 50%, and 40%; overall conversion is 5%. Ten accounts multiplied by $50,000 equals the $500,000 Base-Case annual revenue target. First-deal timing remains 1–3 months.; stages: label: Permissioned opportunities; value: 200 accounts with documented renewal windows; numeric value: 200.0; detail: Count distinct prospective portfolio accounts with an identified buyer, a documented contact basis, and a contract renewal window; exclude scraped contact lists without qualification.; label: Evidence-complete accounts; value: 100 accounts with usable contract evidence; numeric value: 100.0; detail: Half the original cohort supplies invoices, product identifiers, seat counts, commitment dates, and procurement authority sufficient to calculate a comparable incumbent baseline.; label: Eligible economic cases; value: 50 accounts with authorized positive economics; numeric value: 50.0; detail: Half the evidence-complete accounts passes vendor eligibility, minimum retained contribution, and funding checks after migration costs, concessions, and expected clawbacks.; label: Signed mandates; value: 25 accounts with executed commercial terms; numeric value: 25.0; detail: Half the eligible accounts executes a mandate defining compensation, savings measurement, rebate ownership, customer responsibilities, and the permitted licensing route.; label: Activated earning accounts; value: 10 accounts earning $50,000 annually each; numeric value: 10.0; detail: Forty percent of signed accounts completes activation and begins earning contracted consideration. Treat $500,000 as full-year recognized revenue only when service timing supports it.

rect.title: label: Permissioned opportunities; value: 200 accounts with documented renewal windows; numeric value: 200.0; detail: Count distinct prospective portfolio accounts with an identified buyer, a documented contact basis, and a contract renewal window; exclude scraped contact lists without qualification.

label: Evidence-complete accounts; value: 100 accounts with usable contract evidence; numeric value: 100.0; detail: Half the original cohort supplies invoices, product identifiers, seat counts, commitment dates, and procurement authority sufficient to calculate a comparable incumbent baseline.

label: Eligible economic cases; value: 50 accounts with authorized positive economics; numeric value: 50.0; detail: Half the evidence-complete accounts passes vendor eligibility, minimum retained contribution, and funding checks after migration costs, concessions, and expected clawbacks.

label: Signed mandates; value: 25 accounts with executed commercial terms; numeric value: 25.0; detail: Half the eligible accounts executes a mandate defining compensation, savings measurement, rebate ownership, customer responsibilities, and the permitted licensing route.

label: Activated earning accounts; value: 10 accounts earning $50,000 annually each; numeric value: 10.0; detail: Forty percent of signed accounts completes activation and begins earning contracted consideration. Treat $500,000 as full-year recognized revenue only when service timing supports it.

text.title: Assumptions: Illustrative annual acquisition cohort, not measured conversion data. Each stage is a subset of the preceding stage. Ten portfolio accounts each contribute $50,000 in annual recognized retained revenue after full activation; partial-year activation produces less revenue.
